acceptance: Before the switch, tests/parity/cleanup/ holds one fixture repo with: a merged feature branch, an unmerged one, a branch whose leaf is Complete, a claimed branch, a live worktree, a merged clean worktree, a merged dirty worktree, a registry row with no branch, a registry row for a Complete leaf, a specy-road stash and a foreign stash; it records the dry-run action list of `doctor`, `branches prune`, `registry-prune`, `worktree prune <ID>` and `grind-session --delete-merged-branches` on that fixture

Before the switch, a reconciliation table in sr/work/M16.4.1-reconciliation.md fixes the action and reason for each fixture item under each old command and under `doctor --prune --kind` branches, registry, worktrees or stashes; one planner with one merged rule and one live rule (live read from the M16.3.1 snapshot) selects exactly the table's rows for the new form and for each alias; a safety-driven reduction from an old command's selection is a decided row of that table; applying removes exactly the planned items

`worktree prune <ID>` stays as the single-leaf path on the same planner; `branches prune`, `registry-prune` and `grind-session --delete-merged-branches` still work for one release, print one deprecation line naming the new form, are hidden from top-level help and are rows of tests/parity/command_map.yaml
Docs, templates and suggested_prompts name the new form in the same change; the stale-command check passes; goldens differ only for map rows

CHANGELOG.md's [Unreleased] section records each deprecation or rename this leaf makes: old name -> new name and the release it is removed in (the release after 0.3.1 (maintainer, 2026-11-08)); no version heading is written
Estimated net line change (informational, not a gate): package about -300
nodes.title: doctor --prune is the one cleanup path; branches prune, registry-prune and the grind cleanup become aliases
